decision: chose AssetRipper 2.0.0 Linux as the asset extractor instead of extending UnityPy scripts
why: it reads metadata v39 and Unity 6000.3.5f2 and writes a whole Unity project with references kept, UnityPy only gives loose files
evidence: ~/opt/assetripper-2.0.0/ar.log: Cpp2IL Using actual IL2CPP Metadata version 39

decision: found the free AssetRipper gives empty method bodies and dummy shaders
why: premium-only features; these are the two real gaps to fill by hand or by the decode-kit tool
evidence: AssetRipper /PremiumFeatures page, Settings ScriptContentLevel Level3 not available

decision: imported the raw export into Unity 6000.3.18f1 before changing anything
why: need a baseline of compile errors and import time to compare every later fix against

decision: replaced 31 stub assemblies with real Unity/Spine package source and remapped script GUIDs
why: prefabs must bind to working components, not empty stubs; every referenced stub class found its donor class

decision: kept ripped assets out of git and committed tools/rip/regen.sh instead
why: owner asked to keep the public repo small; the 3.1 GB of assets regenerate from the installed game
result: repo 4 MB, pushed to origin main

decision: swapped .NET library stubs (protobuf-net, Serilog, Immutable, Channels) for NuGet DLLs
why: the stubs did not compile (202 errors in import-2) and the real DLLs are free

decision: stopped import-7 and made ripped asset GUIDs deterministic
why: AssetRipper gives every asset a random GUID per export, so regen.sh would break any repo file that references a ripped asset; changing GUIDs forces a full reimport anyway

decision: switched the export to group assets by Addressables bundle and renamed bundle folders to their readable names
why: the flat dump put 43786 files in Assets root, unreadable for people and hard to map to addresses; GUIDs derive from paths so the layout had to be fixed before the expensive import

decision: wrote CatalogDump editor tool that reads the game's catalog.bin with the Addressables package's own internal reader
why: the game loads assets by address; a hand-written binary parser would be guesswork while the real reader ships in the package

decision: M1 gate: import 0 compile errors, 0 missing scripts in the 3 scenes and all game prefabs, first render of lounge sector 9001
why: the asset project has to load and render before any game code or shader work means anything
result: VERIFIED except 23 SRDebugger debug prefabs (scripts not shipped, docs/MISSING.md)

decision: read the game's catalog.bin with Addressables' internal reader
why: need address to asset mapping for game code that loads by address

decision: swapped UniTask, VContainer, UniRx, SoftMask (embedded source), MoonSharp (NuGet), DOTween (DLL + module sources)
why: game code needs working libraries; only paid ones without source stay stubs

decision: wrote docs/TRANSLATE.md and piloted it on NemoLib before fanning out
why: one shared contract keeps many translation agents consistent; a pilot finds holes in it cheaply
